rows.en:
Hold the △ button for a moment, then
release it to perform a
charged melee attack.

Press the △ button while dashing
to perform a dash melee attack.

In Battroid mode, chain melee attacks
while holding Down on the D-pad
to perform a launching melee attack.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).

rows.en:
A launched enemy is left defenseless
for a short time.
You can attack it further during that time.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'keep attacking it during that window' -> 'attack it further during that time'

rows.en:
In Battroid mode, press the △ button
to hit a downed enemy with a down attack.

Please note that Fighter mode
has no melee attacks.
That covers the basics of melee attacks.

Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
rows.notes: review: refit: line break moved

rows.en: Now I'll explain Special Maneuvers 1.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

In Fighter mode, while locked on,
hold the R button to turn
and bring the enemy dead ahead.

In Battroid mode, hold the L button
to guard.
Guarding reduces the damage you take.

Guarding while no enemy is locked on
resets the camera angle
to face forward.

While guarding, press Up, Left or Right
on the D-pad to move
without dropping your guard.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).
Second line break moved to a natural point; count unchanged. | review: refit: line break moved

rows.en:
In GERWALK mode, hold the L button
to hover and hold
your position.

While hovering, press Left or Right on the
D-pad to strafe while facing forward.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856). | review: refit: 'sideways' and 'still' dropped, line break moved

rows.en:
You can also step left or right and dash
while strafing.

In Battroid or GERWALK mode, press the
× button right after taking a knockdown hit
to avoid getting knocked down.

And even if you do get knocked down,
mashing the × button lets you recover
from being down faster.

If you have a wingman, press the SELECT
button together with the D-pad
to issue tactical commands.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'When' -> 'If'

rows.en:
The D-pad left tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on melee attacks.

The D-pad right tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on shooting attacks.

The D-pad up tactical command
orders your wingman to focus
on defense.

The D-pad down tactical command
orders your wingman to unleash
a Special Attack.
That covers Special Maneuvers 1.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'the controls for' dropped

rows.en:
Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
rows.notes: review: refit: line break moved

rows.en: Now I'll explain Special Maneuvers 2.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

Hold the L button and press the ○ button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and fire a Charge Shot.

Hold the L button and press the △ button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and perform a Charge Melee attack.

Please note that Charge Melee is
not available in Fighter mode.

Hold the L button and press the × button
to spend 1 block of the SP Gauge
and perform a Charge Boost.

In Fighter mode, a Charge Boost
hits like a melee attack.

In Battroid and GERWALK modes,
press the △ button during a Charge Boost
to perform a melee attack.

Press the △ and ○ buttons together
to spend 3 blocks of the SP Gauge
and unleash a powerful Special Attack.

Press the ○ and × buttons together
to spend a set number of blocks
and use a Command Skill.

Hold the L button and press the △ and
○ buttons together to perform a
Combo Special Attack with your wingman.

A Combo Special Attack uses
3 blocks of the SP Gauge.
That covers Special Maneuvers 2.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'the controls for' dropped

rows.en:
Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
rows.notes: review: refit: line break moved

rows.en: Now I'll explain how to carry containers.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

Lock on to a container and
move close to it, and you can
pick it up.

You can only carry containers
in GERWALK or Battroid mode.

Press the □ button to set
the container down where you are.

Also, be careful: you can't
attack while you're
carrying a container.
That covers how to carry containers.

Training's over once you bring the container
to the designated point, reach the target
area, or run out of time.
rows.notes: review: refit: line breaks moved

rows.en:
Now I'll explain the basic Real Flight
controls for Fighter mode.

During training, flight mode is set to
Real Flight, and controller settings are
reset to defaults. Please keep this in mind.
rows.notes: review: refit: as row 742

rows.en:
Press Up on the D-pad to pitch down,
and Down on the D-pad to pitch up.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).

rows.en: Press Left or Right on the D-pad to roll.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).

rows.en:
Hold the L button and press Left or Right
on the D-pad to yaw.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).

rows.en:
Press the × button to boost.
You can keep boosting until the
boost gauge is full.

Quickly press Up, Left or Right on the D-pad
twice in the same direction to roll
that way.
rows.notes: review: repeated tutorial line; capitalised D-pad directions

rows.en:
Quickly press Down on the D-pad twice
to fire reverse thrust and decelerate sharply.
rows.notes: review: repeated tutorial line; one rendering

rows.en:
Hold the △ button to
brake and slow down.

In Real Flight, hold the R button
while locked on to swing
the camera toward your target.
That covers the basic Real Flight controls.

All right, go ahead and practice
flying in Real Flight.

Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
rows.notes: review: refit: line break moved

rows.en:
Now I'll explain the newly added special
maneuvers and the special maneuvers
whose controls have been updated.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

With your current option parts equipped,
the option part transformation limit means
you can't switch to Fighter on the ground.
rows.notes: review: term added to glossary | review: refit: 'Fighter mode' -> 'Fighter'

rows.en:
Press the ○, △, □ and
× buttons at the same time
to purge your option parts.
rows.notes: review: term added to glossary

rows.en:
In Fighter mode, with an enemy locked on,
hold the R button to turn
and bring the enemy dead ahead.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'while locked on to an enemy' -> 'with an enemy locked on'

rows.en:
Fighter mode no longer has a Charge Melee.
Instead, it can now perform a Charge Boost
that hits like a melee attack.

Press the ○ and × buttons together
to spend a set number of blocks
and use a Command Skill.

Hold Up on the D-pad while locking on
to switch your lock to enemy aces
or disabled wingmen.
rows.notes: review: D-pad direction capitalised (Up/Down/Left/Right) to match the tutorial convention used in the neighbouring rows of the same screens (e.g. 743, 856).

rows.en:
Lock on to a disabled wingman and
move close to bring them
back into action.

That covers the new special maneuvers
and those with updated controls.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'newly added' -> 'new'; repeated 'special maneuvers' -> 'those'

rows.en:
Training ends when you reach
the target area or time runs out.
rows.notes: review: refit: line break moved

rows.en:
Now I'll explain the
Anti-Missile Action.

During training, the controller settings
are reset to their defaults.
Please keep this in mind.

Hold the × button and press the □ button
to shoot down enemy missiles with gunfire:
that's the Anti-Missile Action.

When you're targeted by an enemy missile,
a Missile Marker appears
on screen.

A yellow Missile Marker shows an enemy
missile that is outside the range
of your Anti-Missile Action.
rows.notes: Source breaks mid-word across the Anti-/Missile Action term; English breaks at natural points, count unchanged.

rows.en:
Once the Missile Marker turns red,
you can shoot that enemy missile down.

You can shoot missiles down
in Battroid or GERWALK mode.

uncertain: rows 809/826/828/840/863/872: the tutorial category rendered 'Special Maneuvers 1/2' and 'special maneuvers'; it should match the MT_030/MT_031/MT_041 briefing titles (rows 634, 636, 642, another slice).
row 803 (and 804): the move that knocks an enemy upward rendered 'launching melee attack' / 'launched enemy'; move name not in glossary.

rows 830-835, 868: charge moves rendered 'Charge Shot', 'Charge Melee', 'Charge Boost' (glossary only has 'Charge Attack' for the generic term). Rows 825/836/838/839 use 'Special Attack' / 'Combo Special Attack' because the source spells the word out instead of writing SP (glossary: SP Attack / Combo SP Attack provisional).
rows 821-825, 838, 870, 871: the allied unit rendered 'wingman' (singular; 'wingmen' in 870 for the generic list). Singular chosen because the player normally fights with one partner.

row 849: this tutorial is voiced by Sheryl (briefing row 639) and only this line keeps a casual feminine sentence ending, so it is slightly casual ('Training's over once...'). 'Bring the container to the designated point' interprets the source verb 'recover/collect at the designated position'.
row 855: 'You can keep boosting until the boost gauge is full' follows the source literally (the gauge presumably fills while boosting).
row 865: 'option part transformation limit' is a literal rendering of a game-system term.
row 876: restructured as 'Hold x and press square to shoot down enemy missiles with gunfire: that's the Anti-Missile Action' to keep three lines; meaning unchanged.
missing_glossary: rows 865/866 'opushon paatsu': rendered 'option parts' (glossary has 'Add-on Equipment' for a different word, tsuika soubi; possibly the same in-game concept, check against the UI).
'chaaji shageki / chaaji kakutou / chaaji buusuto': rendered 'Charge Shot / Charge Melee / Charge Boost'.
